productionReadinessGaps: The channel has one Raft consenter, so ordering has no node-level fault tolerance.
All consortium peers and the orderer are containers on this Docker host, so the current deployment has no host-level fault isolation.

All peers use one shared CCAAS endpoint, and client TLS authentication is disabled; independent organization-controlled chaincode services with mutual TLS are needed to remove that shared trust and availability point.

Per-user Fabric identity selection is now implemented and production fails closed without it; each organization must still provision its own CA, authorized registrar wallet identity, and user enrollments before production transactions can use those identities.
Production enrollment and revocation depend on each organization's real Fabric CA endpoint, TLS root, and registrar permissions; checked-in CA settings are examples, not live services.

The production profile must be populated with real organization-supplied peer, CA, and orderer endpoints plus TLS/MSP CA bundles; the checked-in example values are placeholders and are not deployable.

The channel's committed Raft configuration must be governed and updated to include at least three orderers operated by distinct consortium organizations; configured endpoints alone do not create consenters.
Each consortium organization must provision and govern its own Fabric CA, authorized registrar wallet identity, and user enrollments before per-user production transactions can run.
Revoked certificates are rejected by peers only after the owning organization updates the channel MSP CRL through an approved channel configuration change.
